AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID.description: Azure subscription id (GUID) whose Defender for Cloud surface should be queried. Used as the {sub} segment in the ARM URL path /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.Security/alerts and /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.Security/assessments. The service-principal supplied via AZURE_CLIENT_ID must hold a Security Reader (or higher) role assignment at this subscription scope.

DEFENDER_RESOURCE_GROUP.description: Optional resource group name to narrow the query. When set the ARM URL becomes /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups/{rg}/providers/Microsoft.Security/alerts (and /assessments) so ARM scopes the result to that resource group. Blank / unset queries the whole subscription.

DEFENDER_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional client-side severity floor. Accepts info | low | medium | high | critical (plus the Defender synonyms: informational, important / major, moderate, minor, none / unspecified / unknown). Defender for Cloud's list APIs don't expose a server-side severity filter, so the floor is applied after each finding has been bucketed. Defaults to info (no filtering).

name: ms_defender_for_cloud
title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
description: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (Azure CSPM / CWP) REST importer. Pulls security alerts and security assessments (recommendations) from Defender for Cloud via the canonical Azure REST surface (GET /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.Security/alerts?api-version=2022-01-01 and GET /subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.Security/assessments?api-version=2020-01-01) and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON to stdout. Each affected Azure resource (resolved from alert.properties.resourceIdentifiers[].azureResourceId or assessment.properties.resourceDetails.id) becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because Defender findings live on ARM resources, not on IPs); per-resource alerts / assessments attach as Faraday vulnerabilities — one per Defender object name with [CNAPP] engine prefix. Severity is normalised from Defender's High / Medium / Low / Informational enum (plus Faraday-side synonyms) with CVSS v3 base-score bucketing as a fallback when only a numeric score is present (subassessment-style payloads). Status mapped from properties.status (alerts: Active / Resolved / Dismissed / InProgress) and properties.status.code (assessments: Healthy / Unhealthy / NotApplicable) into Faraday's open / closed / risk-accepted scheme. CVE list harvested via a strict CVE-\d{4}-\d+ regex from properties.additionalData.cve / cves / aliases plus free-form title / description / displayName / remediation token-scan. Refs include alertUri / extendedLinks.href / links.azurePortalUri, DefenderAlertType / DefenderIntent / DefenderAlert / DefenderAssessment pivots, MITRE ATT&CK Tactic / Technique pivots, and CWE-* harvested from additionalData. Resolution is built from properties.remediationSteps (one line per step) with an additionalData.remediation fallback. Auth: Defender for Cloud lives behind the standard Azure Resource Manager control plane and uses Azure AD client_credentials. A service-principal app registration is created in the Azure portal with the Security Reader role assigned at the subscription scope; credentials are exposed as AZURE_TENANT_ID / AZURE_CLIENT_ID / AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET. The token exchange is POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant_id}/oauth2/v2.0/token with scope=https://management.azure.com/.default. Tags: [ms_defender_for_cloud, cnapp, cloud-native-posture].
